title: Reinforcement Learning for Public Safety Power Shutoffs Under Decision-Dependent Uncertainty and Nonlinear Wildfire Ignition Models
summary: Power grid infrastructure is an increasingly significant source of wildfire ignitions and poses severe risks to communities in fire-prone regions. Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS) have emerged as a critical operational tool for utilities to mitigate this risk by proactively de-energizing portions of the grid under high-threat conditions. These shutoffs, however, impose costs on affected communities, and it is therefore essential that PSPS decisions be informed by realistic models of wildfire ignition risk.
